chunks: 1390 - And in another report from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said:
"When you rise from your bed, then look at the horizon of the sky and say: All praise is for Allah, who has returned my soul to me; I worship Him and praise Him.
O Allah, indeed no still night can conceal from You, nor a sky possessing constellations, nor an earth possessing expanse.
Nor "like darknesses, some of them above others."
Nor a deep sea moving along before the traveler from among Your creation can conceal anything; You know.
"The treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal."
The stars have set, and the eyes have slept, while You are "the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting"; slumber does not overtake You.
"Glory be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds."
And the God of the messengers and the Creator of the prophets.
"And all praise is for Allah, the Lord of the worlds."
O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, and turn toward me.
"Indeed, You are the Oft-Returning, the Merciful."
Then recite five verses from the end of Āl ʿImrān, from "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth" to His saying, "Indeed, You do not fail in the promise."

key_terms.التَّوَّابُ: the One who repeatedly accepts repentance
key_terms.الرَّحِيمُ: the Merciful, whose mercy is sought in the supplication
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: praise and gratitude directed to Allah at the start of waking
key_terms.الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ: the Ever-Living, Self-Subsisting One who sustains all
key_terms.الْمِيعَادَ: the promised time or promise that Allah never fails
key_terms.خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ: the subtle betrayal or furtive glance that Allah fully knows
key_terms.رُوحِي: my soul, whose return upon waking is acknowledged as a divine favor
key_terms.سِنَةٌ: drowsiness or slumber, which never overtakes Allah

ai.seo_question: What should a person say upon waking from sleep according to Imam Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a morning supplication to be recited upon waking, beginning with praise for Allah for the return of the soul and affirming His all-encompassing knowledge and eternal vigilance. It concludes with seeking forgiveness, mercy, and tawbah, and instructs the recitation of the final verses of Surah Āl ʿImrān.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1390 - In another report from Abu Ja'far (as), He said:
"When you rise from your bed, look to the horizon of the sky and say:
Alhamdu lillahi alladhi radda ‘alayya roohi, a‘buduhu wa ahmaduhu.Allahumma, innahu laa yuwari minka laylun saajin, wa laa samaa’un dhatu abraaj, wa laa ardun dhatu mihaad,
wa laa kaẓulumaatin ba‘ḍuha fawqa ba‘ḍ,
wa laa baḥrun lujjiyyun yudliju bayna yadayil-mudliji min khalqik. Ta‘lamu
Ghaaratin-nujum wa naamati al-‘uyoon wa anta "al-Hayyul-Qayyoom" laa ta’khudhuka
wa Ilaahi al-mursalīn wa Khaliqi an-nabiyyeen.
Allahumma, ighfir li wa irhamni wa tub ‘alayya,

'All praise is due to Allah (swt), who has returned my soul to me; I worship Him and praise Him. O’ Allah (swt), neither a dark night nor a sky full of constellations nor an earth with layers nor layers of darkness nor a vast sea that flows can conceal from You. You know the betrayal of the eyes and what the hearts conceal. The stars have set, and the eyes have closed, yet You are the Living, the Self-subsisting, whom neither slumber nor sleep overtakes. Glory be to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds, the God of the Messengers, the Creator of the Prophets, and all praise is due to Him, Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds. O’ Allah (swt), forgive me, have mercy on me, and accept my repentance; surely, You are the Most Accepting of Repentance, the Most Merciful.'
Then recite the last five verses of Surah Al-Imran:
Inna fī khalqi as-samāwāti wa al-arḍi ' to Innaka lā tukhlifu al-mī‘ād "
